passage: When deep-sea explorers first found dense communities of giant tube worms and clams clustered around hydrothermal vents, the discovery was puzzling: sunlight never reaches those depths, so the food chains that sustain life nearer the surface cannot operate there. Researchers later showed that the vent animals house bacteria in their tissues that draw energy not from light but from chemicals such as hydrogen sulfide streaming out of the vents, and they pass nutrition to their hosts. The same pattern has since turned up at cold methane seeps. Together these findings suggest that crowded animal communities can persist far below the sunlit zone, provided that ____
question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: the vent animals can survive without their bacterial partners as long as chemicals such as hydrogen sulfide remain in the surrounding water.
occasional scraps of organic matter sinking from the sunlit surface reach the vent communities often enough to feed them.
a dependable supply of chemical energy is present at the site and the resident animals carry bacteria able to convert it into usable nutrition.
the bacteria found in tube worms can also be grown in the tissues of clams under the conditions found at cold seeps.

explanation: The correct answer is C. The passage shows that vent and seep communities survive without sunlight because their animals host bacteria that turn local chemicals into food, so the condition that makes such communities possible is a reliable chemical energy source plus animals carrying bacteria able to exploit it. C states both halves of that condition. A drops the bacteria, which the passage makes essential; B reintroduces the surface food chains the text rules out; and D describes a narrow experimental possibility rather than the general requirement the passage points to.
